newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk Nickel metals exporter gets $50 mln credit.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk Nickel metals exporter gets $50 mln credit.

text.p: Russian trading firm Interrosimpex, the exclusive exporter for the Norilsk Nickel metals group, has received the first $50 million tranche of a $200 million credit deal with ABN AMRO (Moscow) Ltd, Norilsk said in a statement on Monday.
The credit deal, struck in December 1996, involves Interrosimpex receiving four $50-million loan payments, each of which must be paid off within 90 days.

ABN AMRO (Moscow) Ltd is the agent handling the credit, given by a group of western banks for pre-financing RAO Norilsky Nickel's metal supplies for export. The credit will be paid with earnings from metals supply, the statement said.
It also said pre-financing of metals "relieves the situation with payment of current wages and paying off wage arrears."
The company owes its workers 900 billion roubles ($160 million) in salary and holiday arrears and another 1.2 trillion roubles ($211 million) to various budgets.

A union representing workers at the group's flagship mining and metals processing plant in the Arctic town of Norilsk said earlier on Monday it had adopted a plan to call a strike if its demands over wage arrears are not met within 10 days.
